targets.notes: Attaching a CTM walks every word of a recording for every supervision on that recording, building an AlignmentItem list with a linear scan. Words are already time-sorted, so a two-pointer or interval index can replace the nested scan. Measured on four long recordings (80 turns and 500 words each). Median of five runs was 57.327 ms; (max-min)/median was 2.84%.

Merging a session cut concatenates each turn's word alignment with reduce(operator.add), which copies the growing list on every turn. String fields are also rebuilt with delimiter joins. A single extend/chain pass would be linear. Measured on 520 non-overlapping turns with 32 words each. Median of five runs was 10.435 ms; (max-min)/median was 0.90%.

Speaker-count intervals are rebuilt from scratch on every call: each supervision becomes two boundary tuples, which are sorted in Python and then swept. CutSet.describe(full=True) repeats that sweep several times per cut. The timed block is one pass over 300 session cuts with 40 turns each. Median of five runs was 9.734 ms; (max-min)/median was 2.88%.

convolve1d asks next_fast_len for an FFT size on every reverberation. On a cache miss the search walks upward by one and trial-divides by 2, 3, and 5 in Python. A batch of distinct utterance lengths misses every time. The bench clears the module cache and times 880 lengths around 2-3 seconds at 16 kHz. Median of five runs was 30.929 ms; (max-min)/median was 2.55%.
